A man is most in need of his orchard when he is old and when he has many dependents. He is also most in need of his actions on the Day of Qiyaamah. You are definitely right, dear son of my brother.
sources: Abd bin Humayd and Ibn Mundhir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.234) reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haakim (Vol. 3 Pg.542)

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Because Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to allow me in with the veterans of Badr, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) objected saying, 'Why do you allow this youngster in with us when we have children his age?' Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, 'He is of a calibre that you will soon come to know.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) therefore summoned them one day and called for me as well. I believe that he called them that day only to show me off to them. He said, 'What comments do you have about the (following) words of Allaah: ('O Rasulullaah ﷺ) When Allaah's help Muslims) and victory come and you see people entering the Deen of Allaah in droves then glorify the praises of your Rabb (in gratitude for this great favour) and seek forgiveness from Him. Without doubt, He is the Greatest Acceptor of repentance. (Surah Nasr)

Some said, "Allaah is commanding us to praise him and seek His forgiveness when His help arrives and when he grants us victory.' Others conceded that they were unable to comment and others remained silent. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said to me, 'O son of Abbaas! Do you share that view?' When I declared that I did not, he asked, 'Then what have you to say?' I replied, 'The Surah speaks of the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ that Allaah is informing him about. Allaah is saying to Rasulullaah ﷺ 'When Allaah's help and victory, namely the Conquest of Makkah, come and you see people (entering the Deen of Allaah in droves), then this is an indication that your demise is imminent. At this stage, you should glorify the praises of your Rabb and seek forgiveness from Him. Without doubt, He is the Greatest Acceptor of repentance.' Hadhrat Umar sitayitei then remarked, 'That is exactly what I understood.
sources: Sa'eed bin Mansoor, lbn Sa'd, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jareer, Ibn Mundhir, Tabraani, Ibn Mardway, Abu Nu'aym and Bayhaqi both in their Dalaa'il, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.276). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.317)

paras: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Because Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to consult with me together with the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) objected saying, 'Why do you consult him with us ..." The rest of the narration is like the one above.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that he once asked Hadhrat Umar about the verse: O you who have Imaan! Do not ask questions concerning those things that you will dislike when they are made known to you (because they are too difficult to carry out). (Surah Maa'idah, verse 101)

Hadhrat Umar Ja explained, "When some people from amongst the Muhaajireen had certain doubts about their lineage, they said, 'We wish that Allaah would reveal verses of the Qur'aan concerning our lineage.' It was then that Allaah revealed the verse you have just recited."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) about Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) saying, "I know that if that companion of yours assumes the post of Khilaafah, he will be abstinent. However, I fear that he should not be carried away by conceit." "What are you saying, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) exclaimed, "You are well aware of (the virtues of) our companion. By Allaah! He has never changed or spoiled (after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ) and has never offended Rasulullaah ﷺ as long as he stayed with Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Umar asked, "And what about Abu Jahal's daughter that he wanted to marry while Faatima was still his wife (did this not upset Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) replied by arguing, "Concerning the decisive error Hadhrat Aadam (RA) made, Allaah says: ijj-) Itjt ...but he forgot arid We did not find him to be determined (to disobey Our command). (Surah, verse 1 1 5) Similarly, our companion was not determined to offend Rasulullaah ﷺ. The idea was merely a thought that no person is capable of driving out of the mind. In addition to this, people with a deep understanding and profound knowledge of Allaah's Deen are also prone to err sometimes. However, they retract and repent as soon as they are alerted." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "A person will be sorely mistaken if he thinks that he will ever be able to dive and reach the depths (of knowledge and wisdom) with people like you."
sources: Zubayr bin Bakkaar in his Muwaflaqiyaat, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.229).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) when Hadhrat Khabbaab came there saying, "O Abdullaah bin Umar Have you heard what Abu Hurayrah is saying? He claims to have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'When a person accompanies a funeral bier from the house, performs the Janaazah salaah and then follows it until it has been buried, he will receive the reward of two Qiraats, each Qiraat being equal to Mount Uhud in magnitude. As for the person who returns after performing the Janaazah salaah, he shall have a reward equal in magnitude to Mount Uhud'."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) sent Hadhrat Khabbaab to Hadhrat Aa'isha with instructions to verify the words of Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and to then report what she said back to him. In the meantime, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar took a handful of pebbles from the ground and kept turning them over in his hand until Hadhrat Khabbaab returned. When Hadhrat Aa'isha confirmed what Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) said, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar threw the pebbles down saying, "We have lost a great number of Qiraats."
sources: Muslim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.302).

paras: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) said, "We (the poor men of Suffa) had neither plantations nor trade in the marketplaces to distract us frpm being with Rasulullaah ﷺ. All I did was to seek a word from Rasulullaah to teach me or a morsel to feed me (I therefore heard a lot that others did not hear)." To this, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) remarked, "O Abu Hurayrah You stayed more with Rasulullaah ﷺ than we did and therefore know more Ahadeeth than us."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.510). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.332) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "I have never seen people better than the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ . Until he passed away, they did not ask him more than thirteen questions, all of which appear in the Qur'aan (Some of these are): "They (the Sahabah (RA) ask you (O Rasulullaah ﷺ) about the sacred months", They ask you about wine and gambling", "They ask you about orphans", "They ask you about menstruation", "They ask you about the spoils of war", "They ask you about what they should spend". The Sahabah (RA) questioned Rasulullaah ﷺ only about matters that were of benefit to them." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) stated further, "The first beings to perform Tawaaf of the Kabah were the angels. Between the Hajar (Aswad) and the Rukn Yamaani are the graves of several Ambiyaa. When any of these Ambiyaa was harassed by his people, he left them to worship Allaah here until he passed away."
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "The women of the Ansaar were the best of women. Modesty did not prevent them from asking questions about Deen and attaining a deep understanding of Deen."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.158) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bazzaar has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Itqaan.

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) narrates that she was sitting next to Rasulullaah wife Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) when she asked, "O Rasulullaah Should a woman have a bath if she dreams that her husband is having intercourse with her?" "Shame on you, O Ummu Sulaym!" Hadhrat Ummu Salamah cried out, "You have disgraced all women in front of Rasulullaah Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) responded by saying, "Allaah does not shy away from the truth and rather than remaining in darkness about the matters we find difficulty with, we must ask Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ replied to the question by saying, "Bless you, O Ummu Sulaym! The woman should take a bath if she finds any semen." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Ummu Salamah fi exclaimed, "Do women also have semen?" "Then how else do her children resemble her?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Women are but offshoots of men."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.88).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'd (RA), "People used to question each other about certain matters that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned and would then question Rasulullaah ﷺ so much about it that although it had been Halaal, it would eventually be declared Haraam."
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami. 1 Pg. 1 58) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "The verses of Li'aan were revealed only because of the many questions that were asked." When people were posing too many questions to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood he said to Hadhrat Haarith bin Qais, "O Haar bin Qais! What do you think they ask so many questions for?" Hadhrat Haarith replied, "They want to know the answers only to forget them afterwards (they have no intention of putting their knowledge into practice)." To this, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) remarked, "I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship that You are right!"
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.158),
Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.158).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "O people! Never ask about things that have not happened because Hadhrat Umar (RA) use to curse people who asked about things that have not happened."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg, 5 43).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "It is not permissible to ask about things that have not happened because Allaah has already decreed everything that is still to happen."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg. 142).

paras: Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid bin Thaabit narrates that his father (Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit would never voice his opinion concerning anything he was asked about until he ascertained whether the matter problem had already occurred. If it did not yet occur he would not say anything and he would comment only if it had occurred. Therefore, whenever he was once asked something, he queried, "Has it already happened?" "O Abu Sa'eed," the reply would come, "it has not yet happened, but we are preparing for it." "Then leave it," he would reply. It was then only when the incident actually occurred that he would duly inform the people (about what to do).
sources: Ibn Abdul Birrinhisjaami (Vol. 2 Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq relates, "When I once questioned Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b about something, he asked, 'Has this actually occurred?' When 1 informed him that it did not, he remarked, 'Then let us rest until it does.'" Another narration adds that he said, "Then let us rest until it does happen. Then when it does happen, we shall be able to apply ourselves and to get a solution for you."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.500).
Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Aamir narrates that when Hadhrat Ammaar iS was once questioned about something, he asked, "Has this actually occurred?" When informed that it did not, he remarked, "Then leave us until it does. Then when it happens, we shall be able to apply ourselves and to get a solution for you."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.256).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah and explained how much profit he had earned by buying (and selling) the shares of a particular tribe. "Should I not inform you about something even more profitable?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "Can there be anything more profitable?" the man asked. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "For a man to learn ten verses of the Qur'aan." The man then went to learn ten verses, which he reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, 'Should I not inform you of a Surah, the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, the Zaboor, the Injeel or the Qur'aan?' 'Certainly,' I replied. Rasulullaah iS said, 'I expect that you will know it before you leave through that door.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood up and I stood up with him, as he continued speaking to me with my hand in his. I then started to slow down fearing that Rasulullaah ﷺ would leave before informing me about the Surah. As we drew close to the door, I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ The Surah that you promised me?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'What do you recite when you stand up in salaah?' I then recited Surah Faatiha. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'That's it! That's it! Those are the seven often repeated verses that I have been granted and about which Allaah speaks when He says: ijy tf Verily We have granted you (O Muhammad ﷺ seven verses that are often repeated (especially in salaah), and the Glorious Qur'aan. (Surah Hijr, verse 87)
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.220).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Abu Talha is once arrived (at the Masjid) to find Rasulullaah ﷺ teaching the men of Suffa with a portion of a rock tied to his belly in order to keep his back straight because of extreme hunger."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.342).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) was once sitting at home and when some people gathered there, he started reciting the Qur'aan to them. A man then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah Should I not tell something remarkable of Abu He was sitting at home when some people gathered there and he started reciting the Qur'aan to them." "Can you find me a place to sit from where none of them will be able to see me?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "Certainly," the man said. Rasulullaah ﷺ then went with the man, who seated him in a place from where none of the people could see him. After listening to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari reciting the Qur'aan, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "He recites in one of the tunes of the family of Dawood.
sources: Abu Ya'la, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.360). Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.94).

paras: Hadhrat Anas ig relates, "Hadhrat (Abu Moosa) Ash'ari (RA) once sent me to Hadhrat Urnar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, 'How was Ash'ari when you left?' I replied, 'He was busy teaching Qur'aan to the people when I left.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, Take note that he is an extremely intelligent man. You should however never let this reach his ears. How were the Bedouins when you left?' 'The Ash'ari people?' I asked. 'No, the people of Basrah,' he replied. 'They will be extremely offended to hear that (you are referring to them as Bedouins),' I remarked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'Then you need not inform them. They will all remain Bedouins except for the man amongst them whom Allaah blesses with the inspiration to wage Jihaad in the path of Allaah." ' ' ' Hadhrat Abu Rajaa Utaaridi says, "Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) used to come around to us in this Masjid of Basrah and sit in each gathering. I can still picture him wearing two white sheets as he taught the Qur'aan. It was from him that I learnt the Surah ji Alaq). It was the first Surah revealed to Allaah's Rasool ﷺ ,"
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.162).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ left this world, I vowed never to remove my shawl from my back (would not rest) until I had memorised what was contained between the two covers (of the Qur'aan). I therefore did not remove the shawl until I had memorised the entire Qur'aan."
Hadhrat Maymoon (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) learnt Surah Baqara in four years.

A man from the Ashja tribe narrates that when the people of Madaa'in heard that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was in the Masjid, they continued arriving there until almost a thousand people had gathered. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) stood up and bade the people to sit down. When they were all seated, he started reciting Surah Yusuf. The people then started dispersing and leaving until there were only about a hundred people left. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) became very angry and said, 'You want an enchanting lecture, but when I recite the Book of Allaah to you, you start to leave!?"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.256).

paras: Whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) taught a verse of the Qur'aan to someone, he would say, "This (verse) is better than everything upon which the sun rises and everything upon the surface of the earth. He would then say this for every verse of the Qur'aan. Another narration states that when people arrived at his house every morning, Hadhrat Abduilaah bin Mas'ood (RA) would bade them to sit down and then passing by each person learning the Qur'aan, he would ask them which verse they had reached. When they informed him, he would then teach them the next verse and say, "Learn it because it is better for you than everything between the heavens and the earth. In fact, for a person to even look at a verse of the Qur'aan written somewhere outside the Qur'aan is better than everything between the heavens and the earth." He would then proceed to the next person and tell him the same thing, until he had said it to each one of them.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.7 Pg.167).

paras: Hadhrat Abduilaah bin Mas'ood (RA) used to say to the people, "Ensure that you stick to this Qur'aan because it is Allaah's tablecloth (laden with food). Whoever is capable of taking anything from Allaah's tablecloth should do so. Knowledge is acquired only through studies."
sources: Bazzaar, reporting. from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.129).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abduilaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Verily this Qur'aan is Allaah's tablecloth (laden with food). Whoever is capable of learning anything from it should do so because the house most deprived of any good is the one that has nothing of the Allaah's Book within it. Indeed, the house with nothing of Allaah's Book in it is like a deserted house with none to occupy it and Shaytaan leaves the house in which he hears Surah Baqarah."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg. 130).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to a man who very often came to his door, "Go and study the Book of Allaah." The man left and Hadhrat Umar (RA) actually started to miss him. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) met him again, Hadhrat Umar (RA) almost rebuked him. the man said, "I have found in the Book of Allaah such things that have made me independent of being at Umar's door."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Umrnaal (Vol. 1 Pg.2 1 7).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "It is necessary for every Muslim man to learn six Surahs, two Surahs for the Fajr salaah, two Surahs for the Maghrib salaah and two Surahs for the Isha salaah."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.217).

paras: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) Sgi says that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say, "Learn Surah Baqarah, Surah Nisaa, Surah Maa'idah, Surah Hajj and Surah Noor because they contain the Faraa'idh."

Hadhrat Haaritha bin Mudarrib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote to them with instructions to learn Surah Nisaa, Surah Ahzaab and Surah Noor. Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Learn Surah Baraa'ah, teach Surah Noor to your women and give them silver jewellery to wear."

Hadhrat Abu Rayhaana (RA) reports that he once complained to Rasulullaah ticS-f that it was difficult for him to learn the Qur'aan and that what he learnt escaped his memory. Rasulullaah ﷺ advised him saying, "Do not take on more than you can manage and perform Sajdah (Nafl salaah) in abundance." Hadhrat Umayrah reports, "Hadhrat Abu Rayhaana came to Asqalaan where he used to perform Sajdah in abundance."
sources: Sa'eed bin Mansoor, Abu Shaikh and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 1 Pg.224).

paras: Hadhrat Qaradha bin Ka'b (RA) reports that when they were leaving for Iraq, Hadhrat Umar (RA) accompanied them to a place called Siraar. There Hadhrat Umar performed wudhu and said, "Do you know why I have walked with you?" "Yes," they replied, "you have walked with us because we are the Sahabah of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "(I have come to tell you that) You are headed for a region where the people are humming with the recitation of the Qur'aan just as bees are constantly humming. Do not preoccupy them by narrating Ahadeeth before them. They should occupy themselves with the Qur'aan aione and narrate few Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ Proceed and 1 shall be with you."
When Hadhrat Qaradha (RA) arrived at there (in Iraq) and the people asked him to narrate Ahadeeth to them, he said, "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) has prohibited us."
sources: Abdul Ghaafir bin Salaamah Himsi in his Taareekh, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.156).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar Ji said, "Do not preoccupy them with Ahadeeth for it will prevent them from mastering the Qur'aan." Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked the Sahabah (RA), "Do you know why I have walked with you?" They replied, "You have walked with us because you wish to see us off and to honour us." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "In addition to that, I have come for another purpose as well. (I have come to tell you that) You are headed for a region where..." The rest of the narration is like the one above.
sources: Haakim (Vol.1 Pg.102), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: A freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that an Iraqi called Sabeegh in the Muslim army was questioning certain (Mutashaabih) verses of the Qur'aan and continued doing so until he reached Egypt. From there, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas sent him to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA). A messenger brought the letter to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and after he had read it, he asked, "Where is the man?" "He is still on the carriage," replied the messenger. Hadhrat Umar instructed, "Go see if he is still there because I will punish you very severely if he has escaped."

When Sabeegh came, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to him, "What are your questions?" When he stated his case, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar for a branch of a date palm. He then beat the man until his back was scarred. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then left him until his wounds healed. Thereafter, he repeated the treatment and again left him to recover. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) called him back for more of the same, Sabeegh pleaded with him saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! If you wish to kill me, do so in a nice manner and if you intend to cure me, then I swear by Allaah that I have already been cured."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then permitted him to return to his land but sent a letter with him to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) stating that none of the Muslims should associate with him. When this became unbearable for him, Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) wrote back to Hadhrat Umar (RA) stating that Sabeegh had truly reformed. It was only then that Hadhrat Umar (RA) permitted the people to associate with him.
sources: Mutashaabih (plural - Mutashaabihaat): These are those verses of the Qur'aan that are not as clear as the "Muhkamaat" in their interpretation. Their meanings are best known to Allaah. Allaah says about these verses, "None knows their interpretation except Allaah" 3, verse. It is necessary to interpret these verses only in a manner that does not contradict what the Muhkam verses mention. When a suitable interpretation cannot be found, one should not delve too deeply into their meanings because the injunctions of Islaam are clearly mentioned in the Muhkamaat verses and failure to perfectly interpret the Mutashaabih verses will not affect a person's life.

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar states that a man from the Banu Tameem called Sabeegh bin Isl once arrived in Madinah. He had many books and always questioned the Mutashaabih verses of the Qur'aan. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard about this, he sent for Sabeegh while keeping some branches of the date palm ready for him. When he arrived, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him who he was. "I am the servant of Allaah, Sabeegh," came the reply. "And I am the servant of Allaah, Umar!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) retorted. Hadhrat Umar then motioned him (to come forward) and started beating him with the branches until his head was injured and blood started to drip down his face.
Sabeegh then cried out, "Enough, O Ameerul Mu'mineen! By Allaah! That which was in my head has now disappeared."
sources: Daarmi, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.228).

paras: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan said, "Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote to instruct us not to associate with Sabeegh. Therefore, if he ever arrived, we would all disperse, even if we were a hundred people." Yet another narration states that whereas Sabeegh was then despised amongst his people after he had once been their leader.
sources: Khateeb and Ibn Asaakir, Daar Qutni has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when some people met Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar in Egypt, they said, "We have come across some matters in the Qur'aan that we have been instructed to carry out when they cannot be carried out. We wish to meet the Ameerul Mu'mineen to ask him about this." Therefore, when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) arrived in Madinah, these people arrived with him. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) then went to Hadhrat Umar saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen? Some people met me in Egypt and said, 'We have come across some matters in the Qur'aan that we have been instructed to carry out when they cannot be carried out.' They therefore wished to meet you in this regard."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked for them to be brought before him and when they were, he called the one closest to him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "1 ask you to tell me in the name of Allaah and by the right Islaam has upon yott whether you have read the entire Qur'aan." When the man replied that he did, Hadhrat Umar (RA) further asked, "Have you then gathered it all in your heart?" When he replied in the negative, Hadhrat Umar (RA) continued, "Have you then gathered it all in your sight?" When he again admitted that he did not, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Have you then memorised it all? Have you put it all into practice?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) then questioned each one of them in a like manner and after he had finished with the last of them, he said, "Umar's mother should have rather lost him! Do you expect me to make every person steadfast on the Book of Allaah?! Your Rabb knows well that we slip up." He then recited the verse: If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden from, We shall wipe out your evil actions (minor sins) and enter you into a place of honour (Jannah). (Surah Nisaa, verse 31 ) Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked them, "Do the people of Madinah know why you have come." "No," they replied. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Had they known, I would have taught them a lesson with you."
sources: Tabraani and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai (Vol.1 Pg.231). Haakim (Vol. 3 Pg.356) has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) says, "Because Rasulullaah ﷺ was very occupied, he would hand over to one of us any person who migrated so that we may teach him the Qur'aan. Rasulullaah ﷺ once placed in my care a person who stayed in my house, ate meals with me and whom I taught the Qur'aan. When he returned home, he felt that he owed me something and therefore gave me a bow as a gift. I had never seen a bow made of better wood nor more flexible. 1 however went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked him his opinion. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "it is a burning ember that you are hanging between your shoulders."
sources: Abd bin Humayd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai (Vol.1 Pg.231). Ibn Maajah, Rooyaani and Bayhaqi have reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) once taught a Surah to a man who gave him a garment or a shawl as a gift. When he informed Rasulullaah ﷺ about this, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "If you wear it, you will be wearing a garment of fire."
sources: Sa'eed bin Mansoor, as quoted in Kanzul UmmaaUVol.i Pg.230).

paras: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Ubay (RA) taught the Qur'aan to a man, he gave him a bow as a gift.
sources: Baghawi and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai (Vol.1 Pg.231). Tabraani has reported a similar narration but Haythami (Vol.4 Pg.95) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr (RA) says, "When Hadhrat Ubay ig! taught me the Qur'aan, I gave him a bow as a gift. When he went to Rasulullaah ﷺ the next morning with the bow hanging around his neck, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Who gave you this bow, O Ubay?" Hadhrat Ubay (RA) replied, "It was Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi to whom I had taught the Qur'aan." Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, 'You are hanging it around your neck when it is a spark from Jahannam?!" "O Rasulullaah Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said, "But we even eat from their food." Rasulullaah said, "There is no harm in eating the food that was prepared for others and which you ate by being there. However, if the food is prepared specially for you and you eat from it, you will be eating from your share (of the Aakhirah, because of which you will have less there)."

Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) reports that there was a man with him to whom • (1) Ibnjareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai '(Vol.1 Pg.228). he had taught the Qur'aan. When the man gave him a bow as a gift, he mentioned it to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "O Awf! Do you want to meet Allaah while carrying an ember of Jahannam on your back?"
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.232). Haythami (Vol. 4 Pg.96) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Muthanna bin Waa'il says, "When I went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr one day, he passed his hand over my head and I held him by the forearm. Just then someone asked him about remuneration for a teacher and he replied, 'A man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, carrying a bow over his shoulder. Rasulullaah ﷺ was very impressed by the bow and remarked, 'What an excellent bow! Did you buy it?' 'No,' the man replied, 'Someone gave it to me as a gift because I had taught his child the Qur'aan.' To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Do you want Allaah to hang a bow of fire around your neck?' 'Not at all!' the man replied. 'Then return it,' Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer. Haythami (Vol.4 Pg.96) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Usayr bin Amr narrates that the news once reached Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) said, "I shall include those who teach the Qur'aan amongst the people who receive an allowance of two thousand." To this Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "Oh dear! Oh dear! Are people being paid for (teaching) the Book of Allaah?!"

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Ibraaheem narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote to one of his governors saying, "Give people an allowance for teaching the Qur'aan." The governor wrote back saying, "You have written to say that people should be given an allowance for teaching the Qur'aan, but then such people will start to teach the Qur'aan whose only inclination would be to be enlisted (and thereby receive a state allowance like the soldiers of the national army)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote back saying, "Rather give people an allowance by merit of them being family and companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Mujaahid narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) addressed the people saying, "O men of knowledge and men of the Qur'aan! Do not accept remuneration for imparting your knowledge and for teaching the Qur'aan because then even adulterers will beat you to Jannah." (NOTE Since there are also Ahadeeth permitting the acceptance of remuneration for teaching the Qur'aan, a person may do so if he has no other option. While it is best not to accept remuneration, if a person does accept remuneration, he should accept it as remuneration for his time and not for his teaching.)
sources: Abu Ubayd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.229).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates, "1 was sitting with Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab when a letter came to him from Kufa, informing him how much Qur'aan the people had learnt. 'Allaahu Akbarl' Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed (out of happiness). May Allaah have mercy on him. 'They will soon start to have differences,' 1 remarked. 'What are you saying!' Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, 'How would you know that?' Because he got so angry, I left and went home. A while later, he sent for me, but 1 made an excuse. He however sent a message saying that I have no option but to come. When I got there, he said, 'There was something that you had said (What was it?).' 'I seek Allaah's forgiveness,' I said, 'I shall never repeat what 1 said.' It was only when Hadhrat Umar (RA) forced me to repeat my words that I said, 'A letter came to you stating how much Qur'aan the people had learnt, to which I said that they will soon start to have differences.' 'How did you come to learn this?' he asked. I replied, "I read the verse: i J-l-Jlj J Jl Wj 0 From mankind is he whose speech pleases you in this worldly life and (claiming to be a Muslim) he calls Allaah to be witness over that which is in his heart, yet he is the hardest of opponents (to all Muslims). When he turns away (from you) he exerts himself to cause corruption (trouble and mischief) on earth and (among other things) to destroy crops and stock (cattle and other animals). Allaah dislikes corruption. (Surah Baqarah, verses 204,205)

When this happens, men of the Qur'aan will be unable to contain themselves. I then read the verse: When he is told to fear Allaah (because of his behaviour), pride leads him to (commit more) sin. Jahannam will suffice for him (as punishment). It is a terrible resting place indeed. From mankind is he who would sell himself seeking Allaah's pleasure. Allaah is Most Compassionate (Kind) towards His bondsmen.' (Surah Baqarah, verses To this, Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, 'I swear by Allaah that you are right."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.540), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas said, "1 was with Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he caught hold of my hand and said, 'I think that the Qur'aan has now spread amongst the masses.' 'I do not like that too much, O Ameerul Mu'mineen,' I remarked. Hadhrat Umar pulled his hand away saying, 'And why not?' 'Because,' I started to explain, 'when they all start to learn the Qur'aan (without proper understanding), they will start to propound their own opinions. Once they do this, they will start to dispute and once the disputes start, they will start killing each other.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sat aside and left me alone. Only Allaah knows the anxiety 1 endured during the rest of that day. It was only the following afternoon that his messenger came to inform me that the Ameerul Mu'mineen was calling me. When l got there, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, 'What was it that you said?' After I had repeated my words to him, he said, '(I had also understood the same but) I had been concealing this from the people.

Hadhrat Kinaanah Adawi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote to the commanders of his armies to send him a list of all the men who were Huffaadh of the Qur'aan so that he could dispatch them to the ends of the empire to teach the Qur'aan. Hadhrat (Abu Moosa) Ash'ari (RA) wrote back to Hadhrat Umar stating that the Huffaadh with him numbered just over three hundred. Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s reply to him was as follows: "In the name of Allaah the Most Kind, the Most Merciful From the servant of Allaah Umar to the servant of Allaah Qais and all the Huffaadh with him Peace be upon you all This Qur'aan is a great source of reward and honour for you and ssall be a treasure for you in the Aakhlrah. You should therefore follow its dictates and never allow it to follow yours (by distorting its interpretation to suit your desires) because the person whose dictates the Qur'aan is forced to follow shall have it shoved on to his neck to throw him into Jahannam. As for the one who follows the Qur'aan, the Qur'aan shall lead him tojannatul Firdous. So as far as you can, let it be an intercessor for you and never let it be a complainant against you. The person for whom the Qur'aan intercedes shall enter Jannah and the one against whom the Qur'aan complains shall surely enter Jahannam. Always bear in mind that the Qur'aan is a fountainhead of guidance, a flower of knowledge and the final scripture from the Most Merciful. It is by this Qur'aan that Allaah opens blind eyes, deaf ears and locked hearts.

You must also bear in mind that when a man wakes up at night, brushes his teeth with a Miswaak, performs wudhu, says 'Allaahu Akbar' and then recites the Qur'aan, an angel places his mouth on the person's mouth and says, 'Recite, recite. You are doing an excellent thing and it is most excellent for you. ' If he performs wudhu without using the Miswaak, the angel protects him and does nothing else. Behold! Recitation of the Qur'aan in salaah is a protected treasure and an ordained excellence. You should therefore do as much of it as you possibly can. Salaah is a celestial light, zakaah is a symbol, patience is an illumination, fasting is a shield and the Qur'aan is a- proof either for you or against you. You should therefore honour the Qur'aan and never cause it disgrace because Allaah will honour the one who honours the Qur'aan and will disgrace the one who brings it disgrace. You also ought to know that the person who recites the Qur'aan, memorises it, practises on it and abides by its injunctions shall have his du'aas accepted by Allaah. If Allaah pleases, He may accept them in this world and if He wills, he may reserve them as a treasure for the Aakhirah. Remember that what remains with Allaah is better and more lasting for those who have Imaan and who rely on their Rabb.

Hadhrat Abu Kinaanah reports that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) gathered together the Huffaadh (of the army he commanded), they numbered close t. three hundred. Hadhrat Abu Moosa SI lectured to them about the greatness of the Qur'aan saying, "Verily this Qur'aan shall be either a source of reward for you or a burden (in the Aakhirah). You should therefore follow the dictates of the Qur'aan and never force it to follows yours because the one who follows the Qur'aan shall be with it in the gardens of Jannah while the one who forces the Qur'aan to follow his desires shall have it shoved on his neck and it will fling him into Jahannam."

Hadhrat Abul Aswad Daly reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once gathered all the Qurraa, emphasising that none but the Huffaadh should come to him. It was approximately three hundred men who came to him. He then addressed them saying, "You men are the Qurraa of the city and should therefore never allow the passage of time to harden your hearts as it happened to the Ahlul Kitaab. A Surah had been revealed that we thought resembled Surah Baraa'ah in length and in the stern subject matter it contained. A verse from it which 1 had memorised stated that if man had two valleys of gold he would seek to have a third and it would only be the sand (of his grave) that would be able to fill his belly. Thereafter, another Surah was revealed which we thought resembled the Musabbihaat because it begins with the words (Sabbaha Lillaah). The verse from it that 1 had memorised is: (Tc-il) tji O you who have Imaan! Why do you say that which you did not do?
(Surah Saff, verse 2) Testimony will therefore be taken for everything you do and you will be questioned about it on the Day of Qiyaamah."
sources: Ibn Zanjway, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 1 Pg.217).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once addressed the people of Kufa. After greeting them with Salaam and instructing them to observe Taqwa, he said, "Never dispute about the Qur'aan and never oppose each other concerning it because there are no discrepancies in the Qur'aan, it will never be (completely) forgotten and constant repetition of the Qur'aan will never tire one. Do you not see that the restrictions, the Faraa'idh and Allaah's explicit commands in the Shari'ah of Islaam are one? It would be said that the Qur'aan has discrepancies if a part of it commands an act which another part forbids. Every part of the Qur'aan rather complements the rest of it. I am convinced that such deep understanding and knowledge shall surface amongst you people that surpasses all other people. If a camel could take me to a person who has more knowledge of what has been revealed to Muhammad ﷺ than I have, I shall certainly go to him to increase the knowledge I have. I know well that while the entire Qur'aah would be recited to Rasulullaah ﷺ once every year, it was recited to Rasulullaah ﷺ twice during the year that he passed away (every Ramadhaan Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) would recite the Qur'aan to Rasulullaah ﷺ and Rasulullaah ﷺ would recite to him). Whenever I recited Qur'aan to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would approve of my recitation, therefore whoever recites Qur'aan in the manner that I recite, should not turn away and forsake it. In a like manner, whoever recites the Qur'aan in another authentic manner should also not turn away and forsake it because whoever rejects any one of the various manners of recitation will reject them all." A student of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) from Hamdaan narrates that before Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) left for Madinah, he gathered all his students together and said, "By Allaah! I am convinced that such religiousness, deep understanding of Deen and knowledge of the Qur'aan shall surface amongst you people that surpasses that of all other Muslims..." The narration continues until it states that he said, "Verily there are no discrepancies in the Qur'aan, neither does the Qur'aan ever age or lose its dignity by continuous repetition."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.257).
Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.232).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "It is only befitting that a man of the Qur'aan be recognised by his nights (when he is engaged in Ibaadah) when others are asleep, by his days (spent fasting) when others are eating, by his sorrow (pondering about his plight in the Aakhirah) when others are rejoicing, by his weeping when others are laughing, by his silence when others are socialising and by his humility when others are behaving arrogantly. It is also befitting of a man of the Qur'aan to be weeping and sorrowful, wise and tolerant, knowledgeable and composed. It does not behove a man of the Qur'aan to be uncouth, negligent, boisterous, rowdy and short-tempered." Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Do your best to be a listener (rather than always speaking) and take careful note when you hear Allaah say, 'O you who have Imaanf because it is only something good that you are being instructed to do or something evil that you are being prohibited from."

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy narrating Ahadeeth when a Bedouin arrived and asked, "When will Qiyaamah take place?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ continued narrating, some of the Sahabah isB!2ffi!sgi said that Rasulullaah ﷺ (was not giving a reply because he) heard the man but did not like the question. Others said that Rasulullaah ﷺ did not hear the man at all. When Rasulullaah ﷺ had completed narrating Ahadeeth, he asked, "Where is he (the Bedouin)?" "Here am I over here!" the man said. Rasulullaah (Self then said, "Wait for Qiyaamah when a time arrives in which trusts are misappropriated." "How will they be misappropriated?" the man asked. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Wait for Qiyaamah when authority is placed in the hands of unworthy people."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Pg.130).

paras: Standing before the people in the largest Masjid of Riqqa during the days of Eidul Fitr and Eidul Adhaa, Hadhrat Waabisah (RA) used to say, "I was present with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj when he addressed the people saying, 'O people! Which month is most sacred?' 'This month (of Dhul Hijjah) is,' the people replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further, 'O people! Which city is most sacred?' 'This city (of Makkah) is,' the people replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then declared, 'Until the day you meet your Rabb, your blood, your wealth and your honour are as sacred to you as this day, this month and this city are. Have i conveyed the message?' 'You certainly have,' the people replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then raised his hands to the sky saying, 'You be the witness, O Allaah.' Thereafter, he said, 'Those of you present here should pass the message on to those who are absent.' Do come closer so that I may convey to you what Rasulullaah ﷺ said to us."
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.139).

paras: Hadhrat Makhool says, "Ibn Abu Zakariyyah, Sulaymaan bin Habeeb and 1 once went to Hadhrat Abu Umaamah SE in Hims. After we had greeted him with the words of Salaam, he said, 'This sitting of yours here is a means Allaah has used for the Deen to reach you and will also be Allaah's evidence against you (if you do not propagate it). Rasulullaah ﷺ propagated, so you too should propagate."

In another narration, Hadhrat Saleem bin Aamir says, "When we would sit with Hadhrat Abu Ubaadah (RA) and he narrated to us many Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would say to us after he had completed, 'Have you understood? Now propagate as it has been propagated to you.
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.140).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once prayed, "O Allaah! Shower Your mercy on my successors." "O Rasulullaah (illli?!" the Sahabah (RA) asked, "Who are your successors?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Those who will come after me, who will narrate my Ahadeeth and teach them to the people."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.74). Ibn Najjaar, Khateeb in Sharfus Sahabah (RA) and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.240).

paras: Hadhrat Aasim bin Muhammad narrates from his father that he saw Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah come to the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ on the day of Jumu'ah. Standing and holding the two knobs of the pulpit, he said, "Abul Qaasim Rasulullaah ﷺ the truthful and veritable narrated to us..." He then continued to narrate Ahadeeth until he heard the door of the Imaam's room open as the Imaam emerged to lead the salaah. He then sat down.
sources: Haakim, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Aslam reports that when they used to ask Hadhrat Umar (RA) to narrate Ahadeeth to them, he would say, "I fear that I may add a word or omit a word because Rasulullaah ﷺ said, The person who intentionally lies about me is headed for Jahannam."
sources: Ahmad, Ibn Adi, Uqayli and Abu Nu'aym in his Ma'rifah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.239).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says, "I have not seen any of the Sahabah narrate Ahadeeth as well and as thoroughly as Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). However, he was a man who was extremely reluctant to narrate Ahadeeth."
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to say, "What prevents me from narrating Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ is not the fact that I was not one of those Sahabah (RA) with the best memories. What prevents me is that 1 can testify that I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever attributes anything to me that I never stated should prepare for his abode in Jahannam.'" Another narration quotes Rasulullaah ﷺ's words as, "Whoever speaks lies about me should prepare for a house in Jahannam."
sources: Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol. 1 Pg.1 43) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When narrating Ahadeeth to you, I prefer falling from the sky rather than stating something that Rasulullaah Wife never said. However, when speaking to you about matters between us, then (precautions need not be so strict because) wars are won by strategy."

Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon reports that sometimes an entire year would pass by without Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrating a single Hadith. When he narrated a Hadith one day, he started to shiver and perspiration beaded up on his forehead. He then said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said something like that or stated similar words."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.5 Pg.240).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq reports, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) started to narrate a Hadith one day, but as soon as he said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said,' he started to shiver so much that even his clothing shook. He then added, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said something to the effect or something similar.
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.314), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Idrees Khowlaani says, "I noticed that whenever Hadhrat Abu Dardaa completed narrating Ahadeeth, he would add, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said that, something similar to that or something resembling that.'"' Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that whenever Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik narrated Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would end with the words, "It was something like this that Rasulullaah ﷺ said."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. I Pg.141). Abu Ya'la, Rooyaani and Ibn Asaakir have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.3 Pg.156).

paras: In another narration, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrated few Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ, but when he did, he would end with the words, "It was something like this that Rasulullaah ﷺ said."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 1 Pg. 79).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says, "There was no companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ more cautious of adding anything to or omitting anything from the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ than Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA).
sources: Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.240). (4)lbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l44). (S)lbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg,145).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi says, "I sat in the company of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) for an entire year without hearing him narrate anything from Rasulullaah.

Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "I have heard many Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ which I have memorised. All that prevents me from narrating them is that some of my companions may differ with me in the narration."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 1 Pg. 1 4 1 ).

paras: Hadhrat Mutarraf reports that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said to him, "O Mutarraf! By Allaah! I am certain that if I chose to do so, I could narrate Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ for two days continuously without repeating a single Hadith. However, what makes me reluctant to do so and makes me disapprove of doing such a thing is that although I was there when many Sahabah (RA) of Muhammad ﷺ were there and I also heard what they heard, they confuse the sequence of the words when they narrate." Sometimes, Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn would say, "If I were to narrate to you what Rasulullaah ﷺ said, I am certain that I will be accurate." When he quoted the words of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) would do so with great certainty and say, "I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say..."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.141) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Abdullaah reports that he heard Hadhrat Suhayb say, "By Allaah! I shall never intentionally narrate Ahadeeth to you saying that it is what Rasulullaah ﷺ said. However, I shall gladly relate to you what I experienced in the expeditions I participated in with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Then again, I shall never say, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said'."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.229), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal Pg.203).

paras: Hadhrat Makhool relates, "Abul Azhar and I once went to Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa and said, 'O Abu Asqa! Narrate to us a Hadith that you heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ without any uncertain words, and without any additions or omissions.' Hadhrat Waathila (RA) asked, 'Has any of you recited any part of the Qur'aan last night?' 'Yes,' we replied, 'But since we are not Huffaadh, we tend to add a Waawd) or an To this, Hadhrat Waathila (RA) remarked, 'And that is the Qur'aan which you have still not mastered when it has been in your midst for such a long time. When you feel that you are adding or omitting letters to it, what about the Ahadeeth that we had perhaps heard only once from Rasulullaah ﷺ It is sufficient for you that we narrate only their intended meanings to you."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.?9).

paras: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf relates, "By Allaah! Before he passed away, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent messengers to various distant places to summon Sahabah (RA) such as Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir. When they had gathered, he said to them, 'What Ahadeeth have you people spread to even the far distant lands?' 'Are you forbidding us from narrating them?' they asked. 'No,' Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, 'I just want you to remain with me. By Allaah! I do not want you to part from me (here in Madinah) for as long as I live because we know best which of your narrations we shall accept and which ones we will not.' They therefore did not part from Hadhrat Umar (RA) until he passed away."

Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan relates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Ansaari and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and said to them, "What are the Ahadeeth that you are so frequently narrating to the people?" He then confined them to Madinah until he was martyred.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.239).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Awfa (RA) reports that when they used to request Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam to narrate the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ to them, he would say, "We have aged and have begun to forget. Narrating the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ is a very serious matter (which cannot be taken lightly)."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.239).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) both said, "Learn as much as you wish to learn but Allaah will place no benefit in your knowledge until you practise what you know."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Learn as much as you please, but I swear by Allaah that you will not be rewarded for your knowledge until you put it into practise."
sources: Ibn Adi and Khateeb.

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam says, "Ten Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah informed me that they were learning in the Masjid of Quba when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to them and said, 'Learn...'" The remainder of the words are like the narration above.
sources: Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ What will satisfy the evidence that ignorance will hold against me?" "Knowledge," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. "And what will satisfy the evidence that knowledge will hold against me?" he asked further. Rasulullaah Seal's reply was, "Action."
sources: Abul Hasan bin Akhram in his Amaali, as quoted in Jaami'us Sagheer.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Study the Book of Allaah and you will be known for it. Practise on its teachings and you will be amongst its worthy bearers."
Pg.153) has reported a similar narration which states the name of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) in place of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).

Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Study and you will be known for it. Practise on your knowledge and you will be amongst its worthy bearers because soon a time will come when nine-tenths of the truth will be rejected and the only person who will be saved will be one who remains anonymous and aloof from people. Such people are the beacons of guidance and the lanterns of knowledge. They are not hasty, do not promote immoral behaviour or immoral speech."
sources: Ahmad in his Zuhd, Abu Ubayd, Deenowri in his Ghareeb and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 229).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "O men of knowledge! Practise on your knowledge because only that person is an Aalim whose knowledge is followed by practise and whose practise conforms with his knowledge. There shall soon come people whose knowledge will not even transcend their collar-bones. Their private lives will contradict their public lives just as their actions will contradict their knowledge. They will sit in groups, boasting to each other and will get angry if anyone sitting in their group had to leave to sit with another group, The actions of such people will not even transcend their gatherings on its way to reach Allaah."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.7), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "O people! Study, but whoever studies should practise what he learns."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.164) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Pg.131) from Hadhrat Alqama.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ukaym says, "It was in this very Masjid that I heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) begin his speech with an oath as he said, 'Your Rabb shall be Alone with every one of you just as you see the fourteenth moon all by itself. Allaah will say, 'O son of Aadam! What deceived you about Me? O son of Aadam! How did you respond to the Ambiyaa? O son of Aadam! Did you practise on your knowledge?'"

Hadhrat Adi bin Adi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) repeated the following words: "Destruction be to the person who does not acquire knowledge. Still, if Allaah wills, Allaah shall educate him. However, seven times destruction be to the person who has the knowledge but does not practise."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.2).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood is said, "Everyone has fantastic words to say but only those will be successful whose deeds are consistent with their words. The one whose deeds contradict his words shall have only himself to blame." It was also Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) who said, "People are in need of anyone who is engrossed in Allaah. People are also in need of that person's knowledge who practises on his knowledge."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.6).

paras: Hadhrat Luqmaan bin Aamir narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) used to say, "What I fear most about Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah is that he would call me in front of all creation saying, 'O Uwaymir!' Then when I respond by saying, '1 am at Your service, O my Rabb!', Allaah shall ask, 'Did you practise on your knowledge?'"

Another narration quoted Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) as sayjng, "What I fear most is that 1 should be asked on the Day of Qiyaamah, 'O Uwaymir! Did you acquire knowledge or remain ignorant?' If I reply that I had acquired knowledge, every verse containing a command and every verse containing an admonition shall claim their rights. The verses containing commands will ask, 'Did you carry out (what was commanded)?' and every verse containing an admonition will ask, 'Did you take heed (to the admonition)?' I seek Allaah's protection from knowledge that does not benefit, from desires that are not sated and from du'aas that are not answered."

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "None can possess Taqwa until he has knowledge and one can attain beauty through knowledge only if one practises on it."' Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "The worst of people in Allaah's sight on the Day of Qiyaamah shall be that person with knowledge whose knowledge does not benefit him (which he does not practise on)."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his jaami (Vol.2 Pg.10), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol. 5 Pg.243).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "No person will be able to move his feet on the Day of Qiyaamah until he is questioned about four things; (1) about how he used his body, about how he spent his life, about how he earned and spent his wealth and about how he practised on his knowledge."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Pg.90). Abu Nu'aym has also reported a similar narration in his Hilya Pg.214).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.214).

Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.213). Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.21 1) has also reported from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) a narration similar to the one Hadhrat Adi reported from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.223).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) also said, "Learn as much as you want but Allaah shall not reward you for it until you practise on your knowledge."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.3).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Learn as much as you want to learn but Allaah shall not reward you for it until you practise on your knowledge. While the objective of true Ulema (when acquiring knowledge) is to remember (and practise), the objective of foolish people (when acquiring knowledge) is to relate it to others (without practising)."

Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "Hold fast to the straight path and the Sunnah because Allaah shall never punish a person who is steadfast on the straight path and the Sunnah and whose tears then flow from his eyes out of fear for Allaah when he thinks of Allaah. When a person who is steadfast on the straight path and the Sunnah thinks of Allaah and his hairs stand on end out of fear for Allaah, is just like a tree with dry leaves. Just as its leaves fall off when a strong wind blows, all his sins fall off him in the same manner. Moderation when doing something for the pleasure of Allaah and according to the Sunnah is better than exerting oneself in something that is not for the pleasure of Allaah and against the Sunnah. You should therefore check well that your deeds conform with the pattern of the Ambiyaa and their Sunnah, regardless of whether the deeds be an exerted effort or something done in moderation."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg.6).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived back in Madinah, he addressed the people saying, "O peoplel The Sunan have been demonstrated to you and the Faraa'idh have been ordained for you. You have therefore been left on a clear and distinct path, (which you will be able to follow with ease) unless people lead you to the right and to the left (lead you astray). " When lecturing the people every Thursday, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood would say, "There are only two matters of importance. One is a way of life and the other is speech. While the best and truest of speech is that of Allaah, the best way of life is that of Muhammad ﷺ. Everything newly introduced (into the Deen) is a Bid'ah and every Bid'ah is a means of leading people astray. Behold! Prolonged periods (of stagnation) should never pass over you, causing your hearts to harden and distant hopes should never make you negligent (of the Aakhirah) because everything still pending is nearby and something far off is that which is never to come."
sources: Laalkaa'ee, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.97). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his ///Tea (Vol.1 Pg.253).
Ibn Abdul Birr in hisjaami (Vol. 2 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Moderation in the Sunnah is better than exerting oneself in Bid'ah."
sources: Haakim (Vol.1 Pg.103), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi. Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.173).

paras: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "The Qur'aan was revealed and Rasulullaah ﷺ demonstrated his way of life (which we emulated). You people must follow us because if you do not, you shall go astray."
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg. 191) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) once said to someone (who insisted on following only the Qur'aan), "You are a fool! Do you find any verse of the Qur'aan telling you that there are four Rakaahs in Zuhr and that the Qiraa'ah should be silent?" He then proceeded to enumerate the other salaahs, zakaah and other injunctions of Deen, saying, "Are the details of these found in the Qur'aan. While the Book of Allaah only briefly mentions these things, the Sunnah explains the details."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg. 191).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Whoever wishes to follow anyone, should follow the companions of Muhammad ﷺ because from amongst the entire Ummah, their hearts are most righteous, their knowledge is deepest, they are the least pretentious, they are most unswerving in example and their (religious) condition is best. Allaah had selected them to be the companions of His Nabi ﷺ and to establish His Deen. You should therefore acknowledge their worth and follow in their footsteps because they had been fixed on upright guidance."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.97). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.305), as has been quoted in the chapter describing the qualities of the Sahabah (RA).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) used to say, "O assembly of Qurraa! Fear Allaah and follow the path of those before you. I swear by my life that if you follow them, you will go very far ahead and if you forsake their path to go this way and that, you will have gone far astray."

Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that whenever his father (Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas led the salaah (in congregation), he would make it brief together with performing the Ruku and Sajdah properly. However, when performing salaah at home (by himself), he would prolong the Ruku, the Sajdah and the salaah. He would then say, "Dear son! We (the Sahabah (RA)) are the leaders to be followed."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.97). Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Asaakir have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Follow and do not introduce" and his Statement about Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Follow and do not introduce (new ways) because everything has been done for you (Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) have already blazed the trail)."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.182). (3), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "An integral part of the Sunnah is to love Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) and to acknowledge their worth."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg. 1 87).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Be careful not to emulate people because while a man can be doing the deeds of the people of Jannah, he can change according to the knowledge of Allaah and then start doing the actions of the people of Jahannam. When he then dies, he becomes an inmate of Jahannam. It may also happen that while a man can be doing the actions of the people of Jahannam, he can change according to the knowledge of Allaah and then start doing the deeds of the people of Jannah. When he then dies, he becomes a worthy dweller of Jannah. However, if it is absolutely necessary for you to follow someone, let it be those who have died (as practising Mu'mineen) and not those who are alive."

Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari says that someone once informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood about a group of people who sat in the Masjid after Maghrib when one of them would tell the others to recite "Allaahu Akbar" in a particular manner, to recite "Subhaanallaah" in a particular manner and to recite "Al Hamdu Lillaah" in a particular manner. "Do they then do as he says?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood asked. When the person confirmed that they did,, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told him, "Inform me when you see them gathering again."

(When the person informed him afterwards,) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood Ji then came to this group, wearing his high hat, and sat with them. When he heard what they were saying, he, being the stern man that he was, stood up and said, "I am Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. By Allaah, besides Whom there is none worthy of worship! Verily you people have certainly perpetrated a terrible wrong by carrying out this act of Bid'ah! Have you then superseded the companions of Muhammad ﷺ in knowledge?"

A person npmed Ma'dad said, "By Allaah! We never intended to perpetrate a wrong with this new act, nor have we superseded the companions of Muhammad in knowledge." Amr bin Utba said, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! We seek forgiveness from Allaah."

Thereupon Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) told them, "It is compulsory for you to follow the path (of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)) and to strictly adhere to it. By Allaah! If you will do so, you will have advanced far ahead and if you start swerving to the left and right, you will stray far off." '''

Another narration states: "The news reached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood that a group of people were sitting in the Masjid between Maghrib and Isha..." The rest of the narration is like the one above. The only difference is in the following words: "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said to them, "You people have certainly perpetrated a terrible wrong by carrying out this act of Bid'ah, otherwise we the companions of Muhammad ﷺ must have strayed." Amr bin Utba bin Farqad said, bin Mas'ood We seek forgiveness from Allaah and we repent to Him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) then ordered them to disperse.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 4 Pg.381). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration from Abu Za'raa, stating that it was Musayyib bin Nujbah that reported the gathering to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).

paras: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) saw two groups in the Masjid of Kufa, he stood between the two and asked, "Which of you two was before the other?" When the one group said that they were first, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) ordered the other group to join them, thereby combining the two into one. An authentic abridged narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood approached them covering his face and said, "Whoever recognises me will have recognised me. As for those who do not recognise me, I am Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. Are you people more rightly guided than the companions of Muhammad ﷺ The narrator says that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also may have added, "You people are definitely clinging to the tail of deviation." Hadhrat Amr Ibn Salamah says that they were sitting at the door of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood's home between Maghrib and Isha when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari came to the house and said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, "Come with me, O Abu Abdur Rahmaan." When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood came out from the house, he asked, "O Abu Moosa! What brings you here at this hour?" Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) replied, "By Allaah! The only thing that brings me here is something that I have seen which frightens me, yet it seems so good. There is a group sitting in the Masjid with a person instructing them to recite 'Subhaanallah' in a particular manner and to recite 'Al Hamdu Lillah' in a particular manner." Hadhrat Amr bin Salamah says that they accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to the Masjid. When he arrived there, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told the people, "You have wandered astray so fast! Even while the companions of Muhammad ﷺ are still alive in your midst, when his wives are still young and when his clothing and utensils are still as they were! Count your evil deeds, for I stand surety for Allaah that your good deeds will be counted."
sources: Tabraani.
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.181) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Tabraani in his Kabeer. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg. 18!) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: that he once came to his father, who asked him, "Where have you been?" The son replied, "I found a group of people better than whom I have not seen. When they engage in Dhikr, one of them trembles and grows ecstatic until he falls unconscious out of fear for Allaah. (I am late because) 1 was sitting with them." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) instructed his son saying, "Never sit with them again!" When he detected that this did not make an impression on his son, he added, "I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ recite the Qur'aan, and I have seen Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) also reciting the Qur'aan. Nothing like this ever happened to them. Do you think that these people fear Allaah more than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) The son, Hadhrat Aamir (RA) says, "I then realised that what he said was true, after which I forsook these people."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 3 Pg.167).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan narrates that Anz Nujaybi was once standing and relating stories in the Masjid when a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Sila bin Haarith Ghifaari (RA) said to him, "By Allaah! We have scarcely left Rasulullaah (ssss's time and have not even severed ties with our kin, yet you and your kind have already stood up in our midst (to perpetrate such acts of Bid'ah)."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.189). Bukhaari, Baghawi, Muhammad bin Rabee and Ibn Sakan have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.193).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Zuraarah says, "I was relating stories in the Masjid when Hadhrat Abdullaah (bin Mas'ood) (RA) stood up and said, 'O Amr! You have started a misleading Bid'ah! Are you more rightly guided than the companions of Muhammad ﷺ I then saw everyone dispersing from around me until I was left all alone."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.189) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was standing on the pulpit and addressed the people saying, "O people! Accurate opinions came only from Rasulullaah ﷺ because Allaah used to guide him. What comes from us are but assumptions and pretences." Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar then added: ...and assumptions are absolutely useless against the truth." (Surah Najm, verse 28)' ' Hadhrat Sadaqah bin Abu Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab used to say, "Those who wish to exercise their personal opinions are the enemies of the Sunnah. They are too lazy to learn the Sunnah and it escapes their memory even when they do learn it. When questioned, they are too shy to admit that they do not know and therefore use their intellect to challenge the Sunnah. You should beware of such people."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.134).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "The Sunnah is that which Allaah and His Rasool (ic have determined. You should never make your mistaken opinion a Another narration from Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar states that when someone asked Hadhrat Umar (RA) whether Allaah guided him in the judgements he passed, he replied, "Do not say that! That was a speciality of Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Ibn Abi Haatim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Urnmaal (Vol.5 Pg.241).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Beware of asking, "What is your opinion? What is your opinion?' because those before you were destroyed because they asked, "What is you opinion? What is you opinion?' You should also not judge one thing by another because your feet will then slip after being firm. In addition to this, whenever any of you are asked about something that he does not know, he should say, 'Allaah knows best,' because this constitutes a third of knowledge." '''

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Every year is followed by a year that is worse. While no year is essentially worse than another, no nation is essentially worse than another. However, what will happen is that when your Ulema and righteous ones leave the world, such people will come about who will analyse matters using their personal opinions, because of which they will destroy and perforate Islaam."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.180) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.135).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "The basis (of Islaam and the Shari'ah) is Allaah's Book and the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Whoever says anything else based on his personal opinion, I cannot say whether he will find this amongst his good deeds or his sins."

Hadhrat Ataa narrates from his father that when a Sahabi was questioned about something, he said, "I am too shy before my Rabb to employ my personal opinion in commenting on a matter that affects the Ummah of Muhammad.

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to Yemen, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "How will you pass judgement when a case comes beforeyou?" "I shall pass judgement by Allaah's Book," Hadhrat Mu'aadh replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further, "And what if you do not find the solution in the Book of Allaah?" "Then," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "I shall judge by the Sunnah of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ Again Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "And what if you do not find the solution in the Sunnah of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) replied by saying, "I shall then practise Ijtihaad without compromising on diligence." Rasulullaah ﷺ then placed his hand on Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA)'s chest saying, "All praise belongs to Allaah Who has inspired the envoy of Rasulullaah ﷺ with that which pleases Rasulullaah (1)Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.180) has commented on the chain of narrators.

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) needed to pass a verdict and could not find a verse of the Qur'aan or a narration of Rasulullaah ﷺ that applied directly to the situation, he would say, 'I shall now practise Ijtihaad. Should it be correct, it is from Allaah and if it is wrong, it is my error and I seek Allaah's forgiveness for it."
sources: Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi and Daarmi, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.316).

paras: Hadhrat Shurayh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to him saying, "When a matter presents itself before you, pass your verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not mentioned in the Book of Allaah, pass your verdict according to what Rasulullaah ﷺ directed.
