If such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has issued no directives, then pass your verdict by that about which the Ulema are unanimous. However, if such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has issued no directives and about which no scholar has commented, then you have one of two choices. If you prefer to practise Ijtihaad, you may proceed. Otherwise, if you prefer, you may desist from doing so. In my opinion, desisting is the best course for you."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When any of you has to pass a verdict, he should pass his verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not mentioned in the Book of Allaah, he should pass his verdict as Rasulullaah had done. If such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has not passed a verdict, then he should pass his verdict as the righteous scholars had done. However, if such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah and about which neither Rasulullaah ﷺ nor the righteous scholars have passed verdicts, he should practise Ijtihaad. He must then be firm on his verdict without being embarrassed about it." Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "He should then practise Ijtihaad and (when stating his verdict, he must) never say 'I think...' or 'I fear that...' because what is Halaal is clear and what is Haraam is also clear. Between the two are doubtful matters and you should forsake that which gives you doubts for that which does not."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Yazeed reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was questioned about anything and the reply was to be found in the Qur'aan, he would state what was in the Qur'aan. If it was not found in the Qur'aan but Rasulullaah ﷺ had spoken about it, he would say what Rasulullaah ﷺ said. If it was not the Qur'aan and Rasulullaah ﷺ had not spoken about it, but Hadhrat Abu (RA) or Hadhrat Umar (RA) had mentioned it, he would say what Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) or Hadhrat Umar said. However, if it was not found in the Qur'aan and if Rasulullaah Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) had not spoken about it, he would practise Ijtihaad."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 2 Pg.57).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, '"When we receive corroboration (to an injunction), we would not equate anything else to it (and would readily practise it)."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil llm (Vol.2 Pg.57). Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.181) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that when he once questioned Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b about something, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) asked, "Has it already happened?" When he was informed that it had not happened, he said, 'Then grant us respite until it happens and then when it does, we will be able to practise Ijtihaad."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil llm (Vol.2 Pg.57).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says, "I met a hundred and twenty Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. When any of them narrated a Hadith, he wished that his brother (another Sahabi) had done it for him and whenever he issued a Fatwaa, he also wished that his brother had done it for him."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil llm (Vol.2 Pg.58).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "It is only a madman who will immediately issue a Fatwa for everything he is asked." The same statement has been reported from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "It is only one of three persons who would issue Fataawaa; a man who knows which verses of the'Qur'aan abrogate injunctions of Deen and which have been abrogated, a leader who has no alternative and a pretentious fool."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol. 2 Pg.165). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 1 Pg.183).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Uqba bin Umar, "I was informed that you issue Fataawaa to people! The person blessed with the privileges (of leadership bear its burden (of issuing Fataawaa)."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol.2 Pg.166).

paras: Another narration staites that Hadhrat Umar also added, "And you are not a governor (so you need not issue Fataawaa). "
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol.2 Pg.166).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Minhaal says, "When I questioned Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) and Hadhrat Baraa (RA) about selling gold and silver, each one of them told me to ask the other, saying, 'He is better than me and has more knowledge.'" The narration goes on further to discuss trading in gold and silver.
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol.2 Pg.143).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Husayn says, "Everyone now issues Fataawaa on matters that had they been posed to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would have gathered all the veterans of Badr (to consult with before issuing a Fatwaa)."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami Bayaanil Ilm (Vol.2 Pg.166).

paras: When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was asked who used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he replied, "Abu Bakr and Umar. I do not know of anyone else." Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad says that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Fudhayl bin Abu Abdullaah bin Dinaar narrates from his father that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), Hadhrat Abu Bakr IS Hadhrat Umar and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) were amongst those who issued Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ according to what they heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.157). Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaa/ Pg.77).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Attiyya Hamdaani reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood when a person came to ask him a question. "Have you asked anyone else?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) enquired. 'Yes," the man replied, "I have asked Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) The man then informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) about Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari's reply. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) gave a reply that contradicted that of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari is and then left. (When this was brought to the attention of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) He said, "Do not ask me about anything when this great scholar is in your midst."

Hadhrat Sahl bin Abu Khaythamah reports that during the time of Rasulullaah three Sahabah (RA) from the Muhaajireen and three Sahabah (RA) from the Ansaar were authorised to issue Fataawaa. They were Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) (from the Muhaajireen) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) (from the Ansaar).
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.160). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.129).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq reports that from amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah those who issued Fataawaa were Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Zaid (bin Thaabit) Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA).
sources: IbnSa'd(VoI.4Pg.l67).

paras: Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Duayb bin Halhala reports, "During the time of Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) remained the chief authority of the judiciary of Madinah, as well as the chief authority of issuing Fataawaa, Qiraa'ah and dissolution of estates. He maintained this position during the time of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and for as long as Hadhrat Ali (RA) remained in Madinah (as Khalifah before moving the capital to Kufa). Thereafter, he kept the post for a further five years until Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) became the Khalifah in the year 40 A.H. Even after this, he remained instated in the position until he passed away in the year 45 A.H." '''

Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that both Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan used to call for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) (to consult with) and would also consult with the veterans of the Battle of Badr. Until the day he passed away, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Meenaa narrates that amongst those Sahabah (RA) who issued Fataawaa and narrated Ahadeeth in Madinah were Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah Amr bin Al Aas Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA), Hadhrat Raafi bin Khudayj (RA), Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Waaqid Laythi (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buhaynah (RA). This they continued doing from the time Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) passed away until their deaths. Amongst them, the ones who issued the bulk of the Fataawaa were Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah Hadhrat Qaasim relates, "During the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and until the time she passed away (may Allaah shower his mercy on her), (my aunt) Hadhrat Aa'isha IS used to issue Fataawaa by herself. 1 used to stay with her and she showed extreme affection towards me."
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.l 87).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ left us with so much knowledge that even when a bird fluttered its wings in the sky, it would remind us of something he had taught us."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l89).

paras: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Everything that draws one closer to Jannah and that takes one further from Jahannam has been explained to you (Sahabah (RA)). "
sources: Tabraani. Tabraani has reported a narration similar to that of Ahmad from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), which is reported from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 8 Pg.264). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.170) has also reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "I have learnt a thousand similitudes from Rasulullaah ﷺ In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever they (the Sahabah (RA) disagreed about anything, my father (Hadhrat Abu Bakr would come forth with a Hadith that would satisfy them all and settle the dispute. Therefore, when it was asked where Rasulullaah ﷺ was to be buried, no one could be found who had any relevant knowledge. It was then that Hadhrat Abu Bakr 'ig said, 'I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Whenever a Nabi passed away, he was buried beneath the place he lay at the time he passed away.' Similarly, when the Sahabah (RA) posed divergent opinions about the inheritance of Rasulullaah ﷺ, they could find none with relevant knowledge. Again it was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) who said, 'I heard Rasulullaah say, the assembly of Ambiyaa do not leave behind any inheritance. Everything we leave behind is donated as Sadaqah.
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.264).
Baghawi, Ibn Asaakir and others, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Utntnaal (Vol.4 Pg.346).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If the knowledge of Umar was placed on one pan of a scale and the knowledge of all on earth was placed on the other, the knowledge of Umar would outweigh the rest." Hadhrat A'mash says, "I found it difficult to accept this, so I mentioned it to Ibraheem, who said, 'Why do you find this difficult to accept when I can swear by Allaah that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said something even more profound than this. He said, 'In my estimation, nine tenths of knowledge left the world with the demise of Umar In a lengthy narration concerning the demise of Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood stated, "From all of us, it was Umar who possessed the most knowledge about Allaah, who recited the Book of Allaah the most and who had the deepest understanding of Allaah's Deen."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id ' (Vol.9 Pg.69).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "In comparison to the knowledge of Umar the knowledge of all other people seems like it could be buried in a little hole." A man from Madinah said, "When I was presented before Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab, learned scholars appeared to be little children before him. His understanding and knowledge towered above theirs."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.153).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got Hadhrat Ali (RA) married to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), she said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "You have married me to a man whose eyesight is weak and whose stomach is big." Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "I have married you to him because from all my companions, he was the first to accept Islaam, he has the most knowledge and is the most tolerant."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.153).

paras: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), "Are you not pleased that 1 have married you to the person who was the first of my Ummah to accept Islaam, is the one with the most knowledge and is the most tolerant?"
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.102) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "By Allaah! 1 know precisely about what every verse of the Qur'aan was revealed, where it was revealed and concerning whom it was revealed. My Rabb has blessed me with a perceptive heart and an eloquent tongue."
sources: Tabraani and Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg. 101) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to seek Allaah's protection against any intricate problem which had to be resolved without the help of Hadhrat Ali (RA).
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 154).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I know the precise circumstances surrounding the revelation of every chapter of the Qur'aan. If I knew of a person more knowledgeable than myself, I would certainly go to him if a camel or any other conveyance could take me to him." Hadhrat Masrooq says, "I sat in the company of many Sahabah (RA) of Muhammad ﷺ and found them to be like dams. While some dams may quench the thirst of one man, others may quench the thirst of two men, others the thirst often and others will quench the thirst of a hundred men. Then there are oceans that can cater for all the people on earth if they had to settle there. I found Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) to be such an ocean." '" Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) arrived one day at a place where Hadhrat Umar (RA) was sitting. When he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood Ji approach, Hadhrat Umar iS said, "He is a coffer filled to the brim with the knowledge and understanding of Deen."

Hadhrat Asad bin Wadaa'ah reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once made mention of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) saying, "He is a coffer filled to the brim with knowledge. I however had to give preference to the people of Qaadisiyyah over myself concerning him (by sending him to teach them rather than keeping him behind with me in Madinah)."
Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that they once approached Hadhrat Ali (RA) with the request to inform them about the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ.

"Which of them would you like to know about?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked. "Tell us about Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) they replied. Hadhrat Ali said, "He learnt the Qur'aan and the Sunnah and reached the apex of knowledge. This is sufficient for you to gauge the extent of his knowledge." "Tell us about Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) they asked next. Hadhrat Ali said, "He had been thoroughly dyed in knowledge before coming out of the dye." The men asked further, "Then tell us about Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "He is a Mu'min who remembers well after being reminded about something he had forgotten."
"Now tell us about Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) they asked. Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s reply was-. "Of all the Sahabah (RA), he best knew who the Munaafiqeen were."
When they asked about Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "He acquired a substantial amount of knowledge but was unable to disseminate it."

The men further asked, "Tell us about Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) Hadhrat Ali is said, "He acquired the knowledge of the previous Ambiyaa as well as the knowledge of the final Nabi ﷺ. He is an ocean whose bottom cannot be reached and he is also one of us, the household of Rasulullaah ﷺ "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" the men then asked, "Now tell us about yourself." Hadhrat Ali iS said, "It was this that you had intended asking from the outset! Whenever I asked (Rasulullaah ﷺ) anything, I would receive a reply and whenever l remained silent, I would be, informed."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 1 65).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Mu'aadh bin Jabal is certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef (one inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds). He is (definitely) not from the Mushrikeen." The narrator says, "I thought that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) had perhaps made an error because Allaah says in the Qur'aan.- Ibraheem was certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds). He was (definitely) not from the Mushrikeen. (Surah Nahl, verse 120-121) However, when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) repeated his words to me, 1 knew that he meant what he was saying. I therefore remained silent. He then asked, 'Do you know what the meaning of 'Ummah'and 'Qaanit'xsT When I submitted that Allaah knows best, he explained, 'Ummah (in this context) refers to a person who teaches people good things and 'Qaanit' refers to a person who obeys Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. That is exactly how Mu'aadh bin Jabal was. He taught people everything that was good and was obedient to Allaah and to Allaah's Rasool ﷺ.
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l67).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq says, "I examined the Sahabah (RA) carefully and found that all their knowledge could be found in six of them; namely Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit After closely examining these six, I discovered that all their knowledge could be found in Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 176).

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq also said, "When I arrived in Madinah and enquired about the Sahabah (RA), I discovered that amongst those with the most profound knowledge was Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA).

Hadhrat Masrooq reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "If Abdullaah bin Abbaas were our age, none of us would be able to equal even a tenth of his knowledge." Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said, "Abdullaah bin Abbaas is an excellent commentator of the Qur'aan." ''* Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to be called an ocean because of the great amount of knowledge he possessed.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 181).

paras: Hadhrat Layth bin Abu Sulaym says that he once said to Hadhrat Tawoos, "Why have you attached yourself to this youngster (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas instead of the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Tawoos replied, "I have seen seventy Sahabah (RA) who favoured the opinion of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) whenever a difference of opinion arose in any matter."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Aamir the son of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that his father said, "I have never seen as quick-witted, as intelligent, as knowledgeable and as tolerant as Abdullaah bin Abbaas. I saw that when an intricate problem arose, Umar bin Khattaab would call for him and say, 'Be prepared! A most complicated problem is coming your way.' Umar would then accept his opinion on the matter even though he would be surrounded by veterans of the Battle of.Badr both from the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Zinaad narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was suffering from high fever when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) came to visit him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Your illness has certainly posed a great obstacle to us. Nevertheless it is only from Allaah that we seek help." Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) said, "Abdullaah bin Abbaas has been blessed with deep understanding, intelligence and tremendous knowledge. I have not seen Umar bin Khattaab give precedence to any other person's opinion over his." * '

Hadhrat Muhammad the son of Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was once present when Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b stood up and said, "This youth will soon become the most learned scholar of this Ummah. Together with being blessed with intelligence and deep understanding, Rasulullaah ﷺ also prayed to Allaah to grant him a sound understanding of Deen."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.183).

paras: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) towered above others in knowledge just as a tall palm tree towers above shorter ones."
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.185).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il says, "A friend and I performed Hajj at a time when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was the Ameer of Hajj. When he started reciting Surah Noor and commenting on it, my friend remarked, 'Oh Subhaanallaah! What great knowledge is emerging from this man's head! Even the Turks would accept Islaam if they had to hear this.'" Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Waa'il himself said, "I have never seen or heard anyone speak as he does! Even the Persians and Romans would accept Islaam if they heard him."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.537).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) relates, "When I went to Umar bin Khattaab one day, he asked me a question that Ya'la bin Umayyah had written to him about from Yemen. After I had given him the answer, Umar remarked, 'I testify that you are certainly most eligible to speak on behalf of Rasulullaah ﷺ's household.
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg, 184). (4) ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.182).

paras: Hadhrat Ataa says, "While some people used to approach Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas to ask about poetry, others went to him to ask about ancestry and there were still others who referred to him to ask about the battles that the Arabs fought and about their history. He was able to give each group of people due attention and gave them detailed replies to their satisfaction."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 183).

paras: Hadhrat Ubadullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas surpassed all other people in his qualities. He excelled others in his knowledge of past events, in the deep understanding with which he gave his opinion to people who consulted with him, in his level of tolerance and in his immense magnanimity. None knew the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the verdicts of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan better than he. None gave opinions as deeply thought of as he and there was also none who better knew poetry and Arabic as he did. In addition to all of this, his knowledge was also most profound in the commentary of the Qur'aan, in mathematics and in the laws of inheritance. I have also not seen anyone else as knowledgeable about the past events as he was, nor anyone who gave an opinion more dependable than his when people are most in need of one. Sometimes he would sit all day discussing nothing besides Fiqh, while on other days, he would discuss nothing besides the commentary of the Qur'aan. Then there were days when he sat and discussed only the battles of Rasulullaah while on other days, he discussed only poetry or only the history of the Arabs. 1 have never seen any scholar sit before him without surrendering himself to him. 1 have also seen no one asking him a question without receiving the relevant information from him."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I used to remain close to the senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar Sahabah (RA) and ask them about the battles Rasulullaah ﷺ fought and the revelation that pertained to them. Whenever I went to any one of them, they became overjoyed because I am related to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) was one of the Sahabah (RA) with the soundest knowledge. When I asked him one day about the Surahs that were revealed in Madinah, he informed me that twenty-seven Surahs were revealed in Madinah and all the rest in Makkah."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.186).

paras: Hadhrat Ikrama says, "I heard Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) say, 'From all of us, it is Abdullaah bin Abbaas who has the most knowledge of the previous scriptures and also understands best those matters that the Qur'aan and Ahadeeth are not explicit about.' When I informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas about what Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) had said, he remarked, 'He himself has tremendous knowledge because he used to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ about matters that were Halaal and Haraam.
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l86).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once looking at a group of people gathered around Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) during the days of Hajj, asking him about the rites of Hajj. She remarked, "Of those (Sahabah (RA)) still alive, he knows the rites of Hajj best." When the news of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA)'s death reached Hadhrat Jaabir, he hit his one hand on the other and said, "The most knowledgeable and most tolerant of all people has passed away. By his demise, this Ummah has been afflicted with a calamity that can never be redressed." Upon the demise of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), Hadhrat Raafi bin Khudayj remarked, "All the people between the East and the West were dependent on the one who has passed away today for their knowledge." Hadhrat Abu Kulthoom narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was buried, Hadhrat Ibn Hanafiyyah said, "Today the sage of this Ummah has passed away."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg,184).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was regarded as one of the young Fuqahaa."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 187).

paras: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Ma'daan says, "From amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ, there are none left in Shaam whose knowledge is more dependable, who have a deeper understanding and who are more beloved to the people than Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) and Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws.
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Handhla bin Sufyaan reports from his teachers that none had a better understanding of the Deen than Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Sip.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Za'eeza'a who was Marwaan bin Hakam's scribe reports, "Marwaan once summoned Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and, seating me behind his chair, he started questioning Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) as I wrote everything down. After a complete year had passed, Marwaan again sent for Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah and, seating him behind a screen, started asking him the same questions. Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) replied to the questions just as he did the previous year without adding, deleting or even misplacing a single word."
sources: Haakim (Vol. 3 Pg.510), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "Whenever the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ had doubts about anything, they referred it to Hadhrat Aa'isha and always found the answer with her." ' '
Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb says, "Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was one of the most knowledgeable personalities and even the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ consulted with her."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg,189).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Salamah says, "I have not seen anyone with more knowledge of the Sunnah practices of Rasulullaah ﷺ than Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) I have also not seen anyone offer a better opinion when an opinion was sought and seen no one with more knowledge of the circumstances surrounding the revelation of any verse or with more knowledge of the laws of inheritance." When someone asked Hadhrat Masrooq whether Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was proficient in the laws of inheritance, he replied, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that she certainly was! In fact, 1 saw the senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ ask her about inheritance."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4Pg.r89).
Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.189).

paras: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed says, "Although all the pure wives of Rasulullaah knew many Ahadeeth, none knew as much as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA). In fact, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the period of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan This she continued doing until she passed away. May Allaah shower His mercy on her. Senior Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ such as Hadhrat Umar arid Hadhrat Uthmaan iii after him used to send messengers to her to ask about Sunnah practices."
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 189).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "I have never seen a speaker as well-spoken, as eloquent and as intelligent as Aa'isha.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.243).

paras: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) says, "I have not seen a woman as knowledgeable in medicine, Fiqh and poetry as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA).
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.242).

paras: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) once said to (his aunt) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "I am more astonished about you the more I think about you! When I find you to be one of those most proficient in Islaamic jurisprudence, I ask myself what was there to prevent you from being such when you were the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the daughter of Abu Bakr Then when I find you to be one of those most knowledgeable about the history of the Arabs and about their lineage and poetry, I ask myself what was there to prevent you from being such when your father knew most about the Quraysh? However, what surprises me is that I also find you to be most proficient in medicine. Where did you learn this from?" Hadhrat Aa'isha held Hadhrat Urwa (RA)'s hand and said, "When Rasulullaah illness worsened, Arab and non-Arab physicians sent (many medicines and prescriptions) for him, from which I learnt medicine."
sources: Bazzaar, Ahmad and Tabraani in his Kabeerand Awsat.

paras: Another narration states that she said, "When I used these to treat Rasulullaah ﷺ, I learnt all about it."
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.242) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said to his students, "Be people who are the fountainheads of knowledge, who are beacons of guidance, who spend most of the time at home, who are lanterns of the night, whose hearts remain fresh and young and who wear old clothes. In this manner, you will be known to the inhabitants of the heavens while remaining anonymous to the inhabitants of earth." ^ A similar narration from Hadhrat Ali (RA) states, "In this manner, you will be known to the inhabitants of the heavens while the inhabitants of earth will rave about you."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Voll . Pg. 126)

paras: Hadhrat Wahab bin Munabbih narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was informed that some people were debating about predestination at Baab Bani Sahm, he quickly got up and, handing his staff over to Hadhrat Ikrama, he placed one hand on the staff and the other on Hadhrat Tawoos. When he reached the group, they made way for him and welcomed him. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) however did nor sit down and asked them to inform him of their lineage so that he may recognise who they were. When they did so, he addressed them saying, "Do you not know that Allaah has servants whom fear for Him has driven them to silence even though they are neither handicapped nor dumb? On the contrary, they are people who are Ulema, orators and people of high status. They are well acquainted with the way Allaah deals with sinners but whenever they think of the greatness of Allaah, they lose their minds, their hearts are torn apart and their tongues stop functioning. When they recover from this state, they hasten to perform good deeds that will purify them. While they regard themselves as people who neglect their duties to Allaah, they are really the intelligent ones with the most strength (to do good). Although they regard themselves as wrong-doers and sinners, they are really righteous and innocent. What distinguishes them is they never regard anything as being too much to do for Allaah, they are never satisfied to do only a little for Him and they are never too proud of the deeds they do for Him. Wherever you meet them, they will be filled with concern, in awe of Allaah and ever fearing (that they should not displease) Him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) then left and returned to his gathering.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.325).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood ig said, "If the men of knowledge would safeguard their knowledge and give it only to those who are worthy, they would lead the people of their times. However, they have handed it over to men of this world only to receive a portion of the world and have therefore fallen in the eyes of these people. I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever narrows all his worries to the one worry for the Aakhirah, Allaah will take care of all his other worries. On the other hand, whoever has been confounded by the worries of this world, Allaah cares not in which valley he destroys himself."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.243). Ibn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg. 187).

paras: Hadhrat Sufyaan bin Uyaynah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "if the bearers of knowledge uphold it as it ought to be upheld and in a befitting manner, Allaah, His angels and the pious ones will love them. In addition to this, people will stand in awe of them. However, they seek the wealth of this world with their knowledge, because of which Allaah detests them and they have no status in the eyes of the people."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 1 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "What will happen to you when such a calamity overtakes you because of which your youngsters start to age, your elders grow older and such practices are regarded as being Sunnah that when an attempt is made to change them, people will say (about the act is truly Sunnah), This is something very strange!"' When someone asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood when such a time would come, he replied, "When the trustworthy ones amongst you will be few while your leaders will be plenty, when the Fuqahaa amongst you will be few while those reciting the Qur'aan will be plenty, when the knowledge of Deen will be sought for motives other than the benefit of Deen and when worldly gain will be the motivation behind carrying out acts of the Aakhirah."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When a fabricated Sunnah becomes such a norm in society, when an effort is made to change it, people will say, 'The Sunnah has been changed!'" The narration also adds that the time will be "when your Fuqahaa will be few and your leaders will hoard wealth."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.82). Ibn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.188).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "You should understand well that these Ahadeeth ought to be learnt solely for the pleasure of Allaah. When a person learns them solely for worldly gain, he will not even smell the fragrance of Jannah. "

Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked Hadhrat Ka'b (who was learned in the previous scriptures), "What can remove knowledge from the hearts of Ulema after they have studied and memorised it?" Hadhrat Ka'b replied, "It will be greed and asking people for one's needs that will remove it." When Hadhrat Ali (RA) once spoke about certain tribulations that will occur towards the end of time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "When will this occur, O Ali?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "When the knowledge of Deen will be sought for motives other than the benefit of Deen, when knowledge will be sought for reasons other than to practise and when worldly gain will be the motivation behind carrying out acts of the Aakhirah."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol. 1 Pg. 1 87).
Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.6).
Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.82).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed the people saying, "I fear two people for you, the person who misinterprets the Qur'aan and a person who is vying with his brother for kingdom."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.194). Ibn Abi Shaybah has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when a delegation from Basrah that included Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he granted them all leave, except for Hadhrat Ahnaf (RA), whom he kept back for an entire year.

Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Ahnaf (RA), "Do you know why I kept you back? Rasulullaah ﷺ warned us against well-spoken hypocrites and I feared that you should not be one. Inshaa Allaah, (I am now confident that) you are not one of them."
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Abu Ya'Ia.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "Beware of the hypocritical Aalim." "How will a hypocrite become an Aalim?" the people asked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "He will be a person who speaks what is right but then does what is wrong."
sources: Bayhaqi and Ibn Najjaar.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "We always maintained that the one to destroy this Ummah will be a hypocrite with an educated tongue."
sources: Firyaabi, Abu Ya'la, Nasr and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.5 Pg.232).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "What I fear most for this Ummah is the hypocritical Aalim."
"How will a hypocrite be an Aalim, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" the people asked.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "He will be a person whose tongue will be educated but whose heart and actions will be ignorant."
sources: Musaddad and Firyaabi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.233).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "Beware of the places of tribulation!" "O Abu Abdullaah!" someone asked, "What are the places of tribulation?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood replied, "The doors of the rulers. When any of you enters the door of a ruler, he confirms (as truth) the lies he speaks and praises him for what he is not."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.I67).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "At the doors of the rulers lie tribulations just as certainly as there are camels at the place where camels rest. I swear by the Being Who controls my life that as much of their wealth you receive, so much of your Deen will they have in exchange."
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.167).

paras: Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ looked to the sky one day and said, "(There shall come) A time when Deeni knowledge will be lifted (off the surface of the earth)." A man from the Ansaar called Labeed asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ How will this knowledge be lifted when it is recorded in script and safeguarded in people's hearts?" Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "I was of the opinion that you were one of the most perceptive people in Madinah." Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded to explain how the Jew and the Christians deviated from the path even though Allaah's scripture was with them. The narrator says that when he met Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) and narrated the Haditli of Hadhrat Awf (RA) to him, he said, "Awf has spoken the truth. Shall I not inform you about the first thing to be lifted?" When the narrator begged to be informed, Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) said, "It is devotion. It will be so completely removed that you will not find a single person with any devotion." An'other narration adds that a person by the name of Ziyaad bin Labeed who was from the Ansaar asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ How will it be lifted from us when we have the Book of Allaah with us, which we teach to our wives and children?" Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) asked, "Do you know what is meant by knowledge being lifted?" When the narrator submitted that he did not know, Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) said, "It refers to the leaving of the containers of knowledge (the Ulema). And do you know which knowledge will be the first to be lifted?" When the narrator again submitted that he did not know, Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) said, "It is devotion. It will be so completely removed that you will not find a single person with any devotion."
sources: Haakim (Vol.1 Pg.99). Bazzaar and Tabraani have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol. I Pg.200).

Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.152). Haakim and Tabraani have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id.

paras: A similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Of what benefit was the Torah and the Injeel that were with the Jews and the Christians?"
sources: Haakim.

paras: A narration from Hadhrat Wahshi (RA) mentions that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "They (the Jews and Christians) did not pay any attention to it (their scriptures)." (S) Yet another narration from Hadhrat Ibn Labeed (RA) quotes Rasulullaah ﷺ as saying, "They however did not benefit from it (their scriptures) at all."
sources: Tabraani.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once asked, "Do you know how islaam will dwindle?" The people replied, "Just as the dye on clothing fades or as an animal loses its fat or as a Dirham deteriorates when it is hidden away for too long." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied, "That also happens, but the most serious cause will be the death of the Ulema."
sources: Tabraani in his Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.202).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib says, "I attended the funeral of Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit. After he had been buried, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "O you people! Whoever wishes to know how knowledge leaves us, should know that it is like this that knowledge leaves. I swear by Allaah that a great deal of knowledge has just left us today."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.202) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ammaar bin Abu Ammaar says, "When Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) passed away, we sat with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in the shade of a building. He said, "It is like this that knowledge leaves. A great deal of knowledge has just been buried today." Another narration states that as he pointed his finger to the grave, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "It is like this that knowledge leaves. When a man passes away who knows something that no one else knows, his knowledge leaves with him."
Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once asked, "Do you know how knowledge will leave? It is by the Ulema leaving the surface of the earth."
sources: Majma'uz Zawaa'id Pg.202).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I strongly believe that it is by committing sins that a man forgets the knowledge he once learnt."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg. 131). The narration also appears in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.1 Pg. 1 99) and Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 1 Pg.92) .

paras: Hadhrat Qaasim reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The problem with knowledge is forgetting." (S)

Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said to them, "We have been given this knowledge to bear and we therefore pass it on to you even though we do not practise on it."
sources: Bayhaqi and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.24).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa, he said, "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from four things; from knowledge that is not beneficial, from a heart that does not submit, from a soul that is never satiated and from a du'aa that is not answered."
